hero_subtitle: Explore how East Sussex County Council manages public money. £1.89B tracked across 113K transactions.
publisher_bio: This website was created by Tom Pickup, Reform UK county councillor for Padiham and Burnley West and Cabinet Member for Adult Social Care at Lancashire County Council. He is also parish councillor for Clowbridge with Dunnockshaw. Tom builds transparency tools that make public spending data easier to check.

doge_context.political_control_summary: East Sussex CC entered no overall control after May 2026 elections following a Reform UK surge. Reform UK: 22 (+21 gain, largest party); Liberal Democrats: 13; Greens: 11; Conservatives: 3 (lost 18 seats — once largest group); Independents: 1; Labour: 0 (lost remaining 5 seats). 26 needed for majority. Coalition negotiations ongoing.

political_control.tenure_note: Reform UK minority administration since the 21 May 2026 AGM. Cllr Andy Woolley (Reform) Leader, Cllr Pete Morley (Reform) Deputy. NOC: Reform 22/50 (largest), Lib Dem 13, Green 11, Conservative 3, Independent 1; 26 needed for a majority. The 2026/27 budget was set by the outgoing Conservative administration (Full Council 10 February 2026) and inherited by Reform; near-Section-114, balanced only on £70m of Exceptional Financial Support capitalisation against a £55.6m unfunded gap. On High Needs / SEND the council is comparatively well placed: its own CIPFA Financial Resilience Review reports a cumulative surplus of about £2.8m if the statutory override ended, with the override's removal in 2027/28 the medium-term risk.
political_control.source: democracy.eastsussex.gov.uk member index + East Sussex CC RPPR budget 2026/27 (Full Council 10 Feb 2026); verified 1 July 2026.
